examples.en: When I gave her a gift, my grandmother waved her hand to refuse.
It was cute to see him wave his hand and say it was fine.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 저도 모르게 손사래가 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I heard that, I waved my hands without realizing it.
He showed his refusal by waving his hand.

examples.ko: 식당 주인이 손사래까지 치며 돈을 안 받으셨어요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner even waved me off and wouldn't take my money.

examples.ko: 손사래만 치고 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: She only waved her hand and didn't say anything.

explain: 주로 '손사래를 치다'로 쓰고, 손을 내저으며 싫다, 아니다, 괜찮다고 표현할 때 써요. 인사로 손을 흔드는 것과는 달라서 '손을 흔들다'와 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요. 사양하거나 부인하는 장면에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Grandmother waved her hands and said it was fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손을 내저으면서 다른 말을 이어서 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used when you say something while waving your hands in refusal.

phrases.example: 손사래 치지 마시고 한번 드셔 보세요.
phrases.en: Please don't wave it away, and just try it once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 사양할 때 정중하게 권하면서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite phrase used when offering something to someone who keeps refusing.

phrases.en: He waved his hand to say no.
phrases.nuance_ko: '손사래를 치다'와 거의 같은 뜻인데 동작을 직접 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 'make a hand-waving gesture', but it describes the action directly.
phrases.en_equiv: to wave one's hand side to side

explain_en: It is mostly used as '손사래를 치다', meaning to wave one's hands to say no, deny something or politely decline. It is not the same as waving hello or goodbye, so it can't be swapped with '손을 흔들다'. It often appears in scenes of refusing or denying.

examples.ko: 이 일은 쉬이 끝나지 않을 것 같아요.
examples.en: This work doesn't look like it will end easily.
The memory of that day isn't easily forgotten.

examples.ko: 쉬이 포기하지 말고 한 번 더 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't give up so easily; try one more time.
You shouldn't believe it that readily.

examples.ko: 쉬이 잠이 오지 않아서 밤새 뒤척였어요.
examples.en: I couldn't fall asleep easily and tossed and turned all night.

examples.ko: 쉬이 구할 수 있는 재료로 만든 음식이에요.
examples.en: It's a dish made with ingredients that are easy to get.

explain: '쉽게'와 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말투에서 더 어울려요. 뒤에 '않다, 못하다' 같은 부정 표현이 자주 와요. 말할 때는 보통 '쉽게'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 첫 여행의 기억은 쉬이 잊히지 않아요.
phrases.en: The memory of my first trip is not easily forgotten.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쉬이' 뒤에 부정 표현이 오는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, with a negative expression after 쉬이.

phrases.en: He is a person who doesn't give up easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈기 있는 사람을 글처럼 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a written-style description of a persistent person.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 쉽게 풀 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can solve this problem easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 말할 때는 '쉬이'보다 '쉽게'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 쉽게 is far more common in speech.

explain_en: It means the same as '쉽게' but fits writing or a slightly formal tone better. It is often followed by negatives such as '않다' or '못하다'. In speech people usually just say '쉽게'.

t90.ax: You shouldn't believe it that readily.

en: to approve; to consent; to permit

examples.en: My parents agreed to my studying abroad.
The boss approved my vacation request.
She gladly agreed to my request.
After thinking about it for a long time, I decided to agree.

examples.ko: 그는 결혼 제안을 승낙할 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems he will accept the marriage proposal.

examples.ko: 제가 먼저 부탁했는데 상대방이 승낙하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I asked first, but the other person didn't consent.

explain: '허락하다'와 비슷하지만 '승낙하다'는 부탁이나 요청을 받아들여 '좋다'고 답한다는 느낌이 강해요. 윗사람이나 회사처럼 결정하는 쪽의 대답으로 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 보통 '좋아', '그래'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I got my parents' consent for the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁한 일에 대해 허락을 얻었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting approval for something you asked for.

phrases.en: The teacher agreed to my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방이 부탁을 들어줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone grants your request.

phrases.en: My father allowed my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승낙하다'와 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '승낙하다' but used more often in daily talk.

explain_en: Close to 허락하다, but 승낙하다 stresses accepting a request and answering yes. It often describes the reply from someone with the authority to decide, like a boss or company. Between friends people just say 좋아 or 그래.

dis.h: formal; agree to a request or proposal
gh: officially approve a plan or request
boss signs off on a document

p.n: The other word is plainer and means giving permission.

t90.ax: She gladly agreed to my request.

examples.en: The celebrity apologized and went into a period of lying low.
Right now I need time for self-reflection and restraint.

examples.ko: 자숙 기간이 끝나면 다시 활동할 거예요.
examples.en: When the lying-low period ends, he will resume activities.

examples.ko: 그는 사고 이후 자숙하며 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he kept a low profile and stayed quiet.

examples.ko: 모두가 힘든 때라 파티는 자숙하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Since everyone is having a hard time, we decided to hold back on the party.
The city hall asked citizens to refrain from going out.

explain: 잘못이 있거나 분위기가 무거울 때 스스로 말과 행동을 조심하고 활동을 줄이는 것을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '자숙 기간, 자숙하다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 잘못을 한 선수는 한동안 자숙해야 해요.
phrases.en: A player who did wrong must keep a low profile for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자숙'을 동사로 쓴 말이고 조심하며 활동을 줄인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to be careful and cut back on activities.

phrases.example: 자숙 기간이 끝나고 다시 방송에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: After the period of self-restraint ended, he appeared on TV again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 연예인이나 정치인의 사건을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in news about celebrities or politicians.

phrases.en: That actor is currently keeping a low profile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 조심하며 활동을 쉬고 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of laying low.

explain_en: It means holding back on your words and actions yourself after a mistake or when the mood is heavy. In the news you often hear '자숙 기간' and '자숙하다'.

examples.ko: 두 의견을 절충해서 새로운 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: We combined the two opinions and made a new plan.
I talked with the owner to settle on a price in the middle.
Let's each give a little and try to meet in the middle.
It took a long time in the process of finding a middle ground.

examples.ko: 우리 의견을 절충한 결과가 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the result of merging our opinions.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 인기 메뉴는 한식과 양식을 절충했어요.
examples.en: That shop's popular menu item blends Korean and Western food.

explain: 서로 다른 두 가지의 좋은 점을 섞어서 가운데쯤의 안을 만든다는 느낌이에요. '타협하다'는 서로 양보해서 합의한다는 쪽에 가깝고, '절충하다'는 두 가지를 섞은 새 안을 만든다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 두 팀이 서로 받아들일 수 있는 절충안을 내놓았어요.
phrases.en: The two teams came up with a compromise that both could accept.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 두 의견을 섞어 만든 가운데쯤의 안을 말해요. 보통 '절충안을 내다/찾다'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A middle-ground plan made by mixing two different opinions. Usually 절충안을 내다/찾다.

phrases.en: We each gave a little and reached a compromise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말인데 서로 양보해서 합의한다는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that leans more toward both sides giving in and reaching agreement.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 의견을 끝내 절충하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: The two people were never able to find a compromise between their views.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 못하다'를 붙여서 가운데 안을 만들지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -지 못하다 it means they could not work out a middle position.

explain_en: It feels like mixing the good points of two different things into a middle option. '타협하다' leans toward reaching agreement by both giving way, while '절충하다' more strongly suggests making a new plan that blends the two.

t90.ax: I like the result of merging our opinions.

examples.en: The company withdrew the plan it announced yesterday.
I asked them to retract the incorrect article.
The government will withdraw the new policy.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 화가 나서 지원을 철회했어요.
examples.en: He was angry and withdrew his support.
Where do I go to withdraw my application?
The backlash was strong, so he took back his remark and apologized.

explain: 철회하다는 이미 내놓은 주장, 신청, 계획을 거두어들일 때 써요. 신청서나 정책, 발언처럼 공식적인 것에 주로 쓰고, 일상 약속에는 '취소하다'를 더 많이 써요. '발언을 철회하다'는 말한 내용을 없던 것으로 하겠다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Something came up, so I withdrew my application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 낸 신청서를 거두어들일 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for taking back an application you've already submitted.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 어제 한 발언을 철회했어요.
phrases.en: He took back the remarks he made yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말한 내용을 없던 것으로 하겠다고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone formally says that what they said should be treated as unsaid.

phrases.en: Citizens demanded that the policy be withdrawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '철회'로 쓰면 뉴스에서 정책이나 결정을 거두라고 요구하는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun, '철회' appears in news about demanding that a policy or decision be withdrawn.

explain_en: 철회하다 is for pulling back something you already put forward, such as an application, a policy, or a statement. It sounds official; for everyday plans Koreans say '취소하다' instead. '발언을 철회하다' means treating what you said as unsaid.

dis.h: take back a statement, plan or decision
gh: withdraw a lawsuit or formal filing

p.n: 취하하다 is for lawsuits and applications, so it is not natural with a plan.

t90.ax: He was angry and withdrew his support.

examples.en: Famous actors have very high appearance fees.

examples.ko: 영화 출연료를 받고 가족과 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: I got my film appearance fee and went on a trip with my family.

examples.ko: 신인 가수는 출연료가 거의 없다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a rookie singer gets almost no appearance fee.
We disagreed with the broadcaster over the appearance fee.
The appearance fee is calculated per episode.
I donated the whole appearance fee I received at the event.

explain: 방송, 영화, 공연에 나온 대가를 말해요. 강의는 '강연료', 글은 '원고료'처럼 일에 따라 이름이 달라요. '출연료를 받다/주다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I received my drama appearance fee today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 영화에 나온 대가를 받는다는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for being paid for a show or film.

phrases.en: New actors get a small appearance fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금액이 낮다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the amount is low.

phrases.en: That actor donated their appearance fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 돈을 좋은 일에 내놓을 때 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often in news when the money is given to a good cause.

explain_en: It is the pay for appearing in a broadcast, film, or show. The fee name changes with the work: 강연료 for lectures, 원고료 for writing. You say 출연료를 받다 or 출연료를 주다.

examples.ko: 학교에서 오늘 아침에 합격 결과를 통보했어요.
examples.en: The school notified us of the admission result this morning.
The company informs employees of the moving date.
It is a problem if they suddenly announce that the contract is over.
We will notify you of the exam result by email.
Telling people in a one-sided way is not good.

examples.ko: 병원에서 검사 결과를 통보하고 나서 약을 처방했어요.
examples.en: After giving the test result, the hospital prescribed medicine.

explain: 결정된 사실을 공식적으로 알려 줄 때 써요. '알려 주다'와 달리 상대 의견을 묻지 않고 결과만 전하는 느낌이 강해요. '일방적으로 통보하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The company unilaterally notified us that the contract was ending.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일방적으로'를 붙여 상대 의견을 묻지 않았다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '일방적으로' makes clear that the other side's opinion was not asked.

phrases.en: I received notice of my acceptance yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알림을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who receives the notice.

phrases.en: I'll let you know the result by email.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통보하다'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '통보하다' and used widely in daily life.

explain_en: Use it to officially announce something already decided. Unlike '알려 주다', it strongly suggests passing on only the result without asking the other person's opinion. A common phrase is '일방적으로 통보하다' (to notify one-sidedly).

t90.ax: Telling people in a one-sided way is not good.

examples.ko: 회원권 갱신 기간을 놓쳐서 다시 가입해야 한대요.
examples.en: I missed the membership renewal period, so I have to sign up again.
I signed up for a three-month gym membership.

examples.ko: 이 회원권으로 수영장도 쓸 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I use the pool with this membership too?
A friend passed on the membership he had been using to me.
If you have a membership, admission is half price.

examples.ko: 회원권 가격이 너무 비싸서 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: The membership price is so high that I'm still deciding.

explain: 시설을 이용할 수 있는 권리를 말해요. 회원임을 보여 주는 카드인 '회원증'과 달라요. 헬스장이나 수영장에서는 '회원권을 끊다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The annual membership is cheaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일 년 동안 쓸 수 있는 회원권이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A membership valid for one year.

phrases.en: I extended my pool membership by one month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기간을 더 늘릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making the period longer.

phrases.en: I got a refund on my gym membership because I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낸 돈을 돌려받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting your money back.

explain_en: It means the right to use a facility. It differs from '회원증', the card that shows you are a member. At gyms and pools, people often say '회원권을 끊다' for signing up.

t90.ax: Can I use the pool with this membership too?
